method: Full reads of two pinned files with Git blob/SHA256 verification. Executed original AST-extracted original_check against two authored same-size distinct-content temporary files; no deletion or ownership operations executed.
findings: Python formatter writes script to requested stream but JSON report to fixed relative .rmlint.json; script default reads that name in execution cwd. Concurrent generations or moving script can select unrelated report unless user supplies explicit JSON path.

C writer only tests fwrite<=0 rather than full byte count and ignores JSON fclose result. Handler pads object by1024 bytes before delegating JSON methods, relying on opaque layout compatibility rather than a typed embedded JSON handler.

original_check compares current device/inode and size; file bytes are checked only under paranoid. CLI default paranoid is False. Control accepts same-size alpha/omega files with False and rejects with True. This establishes helper behavior, not a removal reproduction.

Duplicate-directory handler invokes rmtree without original_check or recursive revalidation. Empty-file, empty-dir and broken-link handlers similarly rely on prior classification. No such operation executed here.

Main uses latest is_original row as original for following duplicates, rather than explicit group identifier; report validation is weak. Empty list indexing and zero total_files footer truthiness can cause handling errors. OSError is printed and swallowed; final Done message is not an operation success receipt.
Paranoid path uses filecmp.cmp(shallow=False), whose caching semantics need separate qualification for repeated same-metadata rewrites. No cache bypass or final fd-bound atomic check in this helper.

executed_control.scope: Original comparison helper only, temporary files, no generated script main or filesystem mutations beyond fixture creation.

limits: No production-library change or full cleanup-script runtime execution.
